title: Oscar and the Verdict
premise: When Ulyana Marchetti, the cathedral's meticulous archivist, receives a confession letter postmarked the day after a prominent judge's funeral, they realize the crypt that has been sealed for three years holds more than bones. As police close the case as natural death, Ulyana quietly builds their own file from misfiled documents, discovering the killer is someone inside the investigation who has been editing records to stay ahead of them. Racing the start of a wrongful murder trial against an innocent groundskeeper, Ulyana stages a trap in the locked crypt itself, forcing the true killer—a cathedral canon protecting decades of financial corruption—to confess on record. The verdict comes not from the court but from the archive: truth preserved, at the cost of Ulyana's invisibility.
about_author: Quentin Joubert is a former parish records clerk in provincial France who spent a decade cataloguing documents no one was supposed to read. He writes mysteries about quiet people who know too much, and lives under a name that isn't quite his own.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of the Dead
chapters.summary: Ulyana Marchetti's POV. We meet the archivist cataloguing funeral registers in the cathedral of Saint-Aubin, establishing their obsessive order and deliberate invisibility. The town mourns Judge Édouard Renard, buried three days ago. Emotional beat: comfort found in routine—until Ulyana notices the crypt key log shows an entry dated after the burial.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. An unsigned letter arrives confessing to Renard's murder, postmarked the day after the funeral. Police have already ruled natural death; the letter names the sealed crypt. Ulyana must decide whether to hand it over or investigate alone. Emotional beat: fear curdling into a strange, thrilling sense of purpose.

chapters.title: Three Years Sealed
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, with flashbacks. The history of the crypt's locking after a fire three years ago—and the suspicious speed with which Canon Vasseur ordered it sealed. Ulyana maps what records went missing in those weeks. Emotional beat: the dawning realization that the archive itself has been curated by someone else's hands.

chapters.title: The Detective Who Files Too Neatly
chapters.summary: Dual POV begins: Inspector Solène Brac introduces herself, reopening the case quietly. She interviews Ulyana and notices the archivist knows the file better than she does. Mutual suspicion sparks. Emotional beat: two careful people recognizing each other as threats—or allies.

chapters.title: Misfiled
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Hunting for Renard's donation ledgers, Ulyana finds pages subtly renumbered—an archivist's nightmare and a forger's signature. Someone inside has been editing history for years. Emotional beat: violation; the sanctuary of order desecrated.

chapters.title: The Groundskeeper's Alibi
chapters.summary: Solène's POV. A anonymous tip implicates groundskeeper Marek Dolz, whose prints are on the crypt gate. Solène doubts it—the tip is too precise, quoting case details never made public. Emotional beat: professional unease deepening into dread that the leak is internal.

chapters.title: What the Fire Didn't Burn
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. In the diocesan offsite storage, Ulyana finds the pre-fire financial records: Renard had been auditing the cathedral restoration fund before his death. Emotional beat: cold clarity—the motive is money laundered through stone and stained glass.

chapters.title: Canon Vasseur's Kindness
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Vasseur offers Ulyana a promotion and gentle warnings about 'obsessing over paper.' Charm laced with menace. Ulyana accepts the promotion to buy access while hiding everything they know. Emotional beat: the corrupting taste of complicity—loyalty offered at the price of silence.

chapters.title: A Trial Date Is Set
chapters.summary: Solène's POV. The prosecutor charges Marek Dolz; trial begins in five weeks. Solène's superior orders her to stop pulling threads. She visits Ulyana after hours, and they form a wary, deniable alliance. Emotional beat: the clock starts; isolation ends.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Another letter arrives—this one addressed to Ulyana by name, describing their own movements with unsettling accuracy. The killer knows exactly who is reading. Emotional beat: terror and a perverse flattery; invisibility was never real.

chapters.title: Ledgers in Latin
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Decoding Renard's coded marginalia, Ulyana and Solène trace payments to a shell company tied to the restoration fund—and to signatures of every trustee, including Vasseur. Emotional beat: the intoxication of almost knowing, undercut by how high the conspiracy reaches.

chapters.title: Marek in the Visiting Room
chapters.summary: Solène's POV. Interviewing Dolz, Solène finds a man who saw something in the crypt the night of the fire and was paid to forget. He'll only talk if his sister is protected. Emotional beat: compassion sharpening Solène's resolve; the innocent face of the machine's gears.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The offsite storage unit burns overnight. Ulyana barely escapes with one ledger page smuggled in a coat lining. The message is unmistakable. Emotional beat: grief for the archive, and the first moment Ulyana truly fears for their life.

chapters.title: The Confession That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Solène's POV. Forensics date the first confession letter's ink and paper—it was written before Renard died. The letters aren't confessions; they're bait, designed to draw out whoever kept reading. Someone wanted this investigated. Emotional beat: vertigo—the case flips inside out.

chapters.title: Renard's Last Filing
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Reconstructing the judge's final weeks, Ulyana realizes Renard mailed the letters himself before dying—anticipating his own murder and trusting only the archivist's obsession with order to find them. Emotional beat: awe and sorrow; a dead man's faith in a stranger.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Ledger
chapters.summary: Vasseur's POV (first time). The canon reflects on thirty years of protecting the church's money and its people, convinced he is the faithful one. He decides Ulyana must be handled. Emotional beat: chilling self-righteousness—corruption wearing vestments.

chapters.title: The Trap in the Crypt
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Solène plan: reopen the crypt officially for a 'records audit,' seed it with forged evidence of the shell company, and let the killer come to destroy it. Every detail rehearsed like a liturgy. Emotional beat: terrified exhilaration; the invisible becoming the lure.

chapters.title: Night of the Locked Door
chapters.summary: Climax part one. In the crypt after dark, the trap springs—but not on Vasseur. His fixer, the cathedral's own facilities manager, comes instead, and turns on Ulyana. Solène intervenes; a brutal struggle among the tombs. Emotional beat: raw survival; plans meeting flesh.

chapters.title: Verdict Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Climax part two. With the fixer arrested and recorded, Ulyana confronts Vasseur privately with the reconstructed ledger—not to forgive, but to make him choose: confess publicly or be archived forever. He breaks, recanting on tape as the trial opens. Emotional beat: justice seized, not granted; power reclaimed by paper.

chapters.title: The Trial Begins
chapters.summary: Solène's POV. Dolz walks free as the case collapses; Vasseur is charged amid scandal. Solène testifies to methods she can't fully explain, protecting Ulyana's role. Emotional beat: bittersweet vindication—the law arriving late to a truth won elsewhere.

chapters.title: Recatalogued
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana restores the tampered files, entering Renard's letters into the permanent record under his own name at last. The crypt is unsealed; light enters. Emotional beat: mourning transmuted into memorial; order restored honestly.

chapters.title: Oscar Signs the Register
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Ulyana's POV. Revealed: Oscar is the name Ulyana abandoned years ago, signed now for the first time in the visitors' register. A new anonymous letter arrives—another town, another secret—but this time Ulyana smiles. Emotional beat: rebirth; the invisible choosing, finally, to be seen.
